clue.text: Some can't get none of this legal payment

definitions.text: Some can't get none of this
definitions.meaning: a jokey nod to the Rolling Stones song (I Can't Get No) ...
in law, the paying off of a debt or claim is its discharge or settlement

explanation.walkthrough: The first half alludes to the Rolling Stones hit '(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction', its double negative reworded.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is a song-title allusion; in law the word also means settlement of a debt or claim.

clue.text: Pen with point I coloured — there's no flow with it

parts.note: a pen for pigs is a sty
C is a standard abbreviation for coloured

explanation.surface: A writer describes a coloured pen whose ink refuses to flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic substance stops bleeding, so blood will not flow with it applied.

clue.text: Chuck briefly dons excellent headgear

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the shortened word wears the other piece inside it
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to chuck is to toss
phat is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone called Chuck briefly puts on some fine hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name but is the verb to throw; PHAT is street slang, and 'dons' wraps the shortened throw around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall formal silk hats are a classic kind of headgear.

clue.text: Supplier's first to stop advert for engine component

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to park a car is to stop it
a plug is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A supplier is first in line to ban an advert for some engine part.
explanation.definitionFit: The igniting device in a petrol engine's cylinder is one of its components.

clue.text: Girl lifted something worth having

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl was lifted up as a prized possession.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable possession or quality, something it pays to have.

clue.text: Four o'clock, say, and char issue is raised

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: At four o'clock somebody brings up a matter about the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Four o'clock is an example of the hour for an afternoon cuppa in Britain.

clue.text: A part of soil's kind of waterproof

indicators.note: A part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that part of some kind of soil keeps out water.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'of waterproof' is changed to 'waterproof': 'of' is a link word, and 'soil's kind' holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a garment made of oiled cloth, a waterproof coat.

clue.text: Stop occasion that gets unruly

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone wants to halt an event that is turning rowdy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb but is a noun: a place where coaches stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot where long-distance buses halt is a stop on their route.

clue.text: A place to exhibit high heavenly home

definitions.meaning: the London exhibition hall at Kensington
the ancient Greek sanctuary of Zeus, chief of the gods

explanation.walkthrough: Olympia in west London is a major exhibition centre; ancient Olympia in Greece was sacred to Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a London exhibition venue and to the Greek holy site of Zeus.

clue.text: Small ring round front of popular company's logo

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
O is round in shape

indicators.note: front of takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A small circle around the front of a popular firm's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The company is Shell, whose logo is a shell of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell's emblem is a ribbed bivalve shell, so this shellfish is that company's logo.

clue.text: Crowd catch an official statement

parts.note: to crowd is to press in
a release is a catch that frees a mechanism

explanation.surface: A crowd snatches an official announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement issued to journalists is an official statement.

clue.text: Women in California natter on runway

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to natter is to talk

explanation.surface: Women in California chat about a fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised walkway models parade along is called a runway in American English.

clue.text: Call round with a wink

indicators.note: round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a tinkle is British slang for a phone call

explanation.surface: Someone calls round with a knowing wink.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkle is a brief flash or blink, as in a twinkle of the eye.

clue.text: Gets rid of jazzman's instrument, as listener implies

indicators.note: a listener hears rather than reads, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: the sax is a jazz musician's instrument

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a jazz player's instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack is to dismiss from a job, getting rid of a worker.

clue.text: Solo needs to be tied up … as do these

definitions.text: Solo needs to be tied up … as do these

indicators.note: being tied up in knots suggests the letters are tangled into new order

explanation.surface: A solo performer needs tying up, like other unfinished matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: unfinished details are what need tying up.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfinished details are proverbially tied up, so they need to be tied up like the solo.

clue.text: Bay resort could be the place for this eatery

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A seaside resort by a bay might be ideal for a seafood restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant serving shellfish is an eatery.

clue.text: A box and a grand American vegetable

parts.note: to box is to spar
G is slang for grand, a thousand
US means American

explanation.surface: Someone buys a box and a big American vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus spears are a green vegetable.

clue.text: Medicine's rank stink

parts.note: a rank is a place in order
BO, body odour, is a stink

explanation.surface: A medicine's foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective meaning smelly but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medicine given for its psychological effect.

clue.text: Fruit is evident in storm season primarily

indicators.note: evident in means the word appears within the other

parts.note: a rainstorm brings rain

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Fruit shows up in the stormy season.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried grapes are a fruit.

clue.text: Bit of brass to annoy the French

parts.note: to bug is to annoy
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A piece of brass annoys the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass instrument used for military calls.

clue.text: Put up with copper beginning to berate youngster?

parts.note: to bear is to put up with
CU is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Tolerating a policeman who starts telling off a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: a young animal, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bear is a youngster among animals.

clue.text: Opening with the old stare

parts.note: a glade is an opening in a forest
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: An opening comes with an old-fashioned stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirtatious or amorous look is called a glad eye.

clue.text: Peace song's fancy picture

definitions.meaning: the John Lennon song about world peace

explanation.definitionFit: Lennon's peace anthem shares its title with the verb meaning to envisage or suppose.

clue.text: A pair of journos (good at heart) with the ability to cut

indicators.note: at heart means put in the middle
a pair of means the piece is used twice

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Two journalists, good at heart, can cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An edged blade has a sharp edge and so can cut.

clue.text: Send out electronic order? Date's not specified

indicators.note: not specified says the letter is left out

parts.note: a mandate is an order
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: Sending an online order but leaving the date blank.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or send out.

clue.text: Requiring a baker's job to be expressed

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: a baker kneads dough

explanation.surface: A baker's work must be talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Needing something is wanting or requiring it.

clue.text: Loads of castle-builders!

definitions.meaning: pails used to mould sandcastles on the beach

explanation.definitionFit: It rains in great quantity, and children use pails for sandcastles.

clue.text: Excitedly describe loan of some importance

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly describes a loan that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means sizable or notable, so of some importance.
